guide_description: One day centered on the twin historic nuclei of Amalfi and Atrani - the medieval maritime republic's cathedral, its hidden paper mill valley, and its smallest neighbor tucked around the headland. Ravello sits above as an optional elevation escape. The day builds from the cathedral square outward along the coast and up into the hills.

days.cluster_tagline: A medieval maritime republic squeezed between cliffs and sea - cathedral, paper mills, and a hidden fishing square
days.neighborhood_description: Amalfi was once a naval power rivaling Venice and Genoa, minting its own currency and writing maritime law codes still referenced today. The town is compressed into a narrow valley where the Canneto stream meets the Tyrrhenian Sea, with lanes that dead-end into staircases and paper mills clinging to the gorge walls. Atrani, a five-minute walk east around the cliff, is technically a separate comune - the smallest in Italy by area - and retains a working fishing-village character largely free of the main tourist flow.

morning.notes: Arrive before 9:30am when tour buses from Naples and Sorrento begin unloading - the Piazza del Duomo transforms from a quiet square into a crowd bottleneck within minutes of the first coaches arriving. The interlaced Arab-Norman geometric decoration on the facade is unique in southern Italy and reflects Amalfi's direct trade with the Arab world in the 10th and 11th centuries. The entry ticket includes the 9th-century crypt of Saint Andrew, where the mosaic program is better preserved than anything in the upper church.

walk_to_next.to: Valle dei Mulini - Paper Mill Valley

afternoon.activity_title: Valle dei Mulini - Museo della Carta
afternoon.notes: Walk straight up Via Lorenzo d'Amalfi past the duomo and keep going - the street narrows into the Canneto valley gorge and the air cools noticeably within three minutes. The paper museum occupies a 13th-century mill still using original hydraulic hammers; the working demonstration takes about twenty minutes and is the most specific reason to visit the Amalfi valley rather than just the coast. Amalfi produced some of the earliest European paper, and the mill explains the technology via Arabic transmission rather than Chinese directly.

evening.activity_title: Atrani - Piazza Umberto I and Santa Maria Maddalena
evening.notes: Follow the seafront path east from Amalfi harbor - it rounds the cliff and drops into Atrani's tiny beach square in about twelve minutes on foot, bypassing the coast road entirely. The square sits almost at sea level, surrounded by stacked houses, and faces directly west so the sunset light hits the church facade and the fishing boats simultaneously. Atrani has almost no souvenir shops; the bar on the square serves the same aperitivo as Amalfi at roughly half the price.

if_time_permits.notes: Take the SITA bus from Amalfi's main piazza up to Ravello - the journey takes about 25 minutes on hairpin roads and is itself a reason to go. Villa Rufolo's belvedere terrace overhangs the cliff at 365 meters and gives the most photographed panorama on the entire coast; Wagner visited in 1880 and declared it the garden of Klingsor from Parsifal. Come early before the terrace fills - the garden itself is small and a single tour group makes it feel crowded.

if_time_permits.activity_title: Fontana Sant'Andrea and the medieval lanes
if_time_permits.notes: From the duomo steps, take the covered staircase vaulted passage to the left of the campanile - it leads into the older residential core of Amalfi, above and behind the tourist-facing piazza. The lanes here are covered with barrel vaults that were originally individual family compounds; the city grew vertically rather than horizontally because there was no flat ground. Within two minutes of leaving the piazza you are almost entirely alone.
